newsitem.title: UK: George says BoE must continue to monitor UK banks.
newsitem.headline: George says BoE must continue to monitor UK banks.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Tuesday it will be important for the Bank to continue monitoring Britain's financial institutions under the new regulatory regime.
George welcomed the appointment of his deputy, Howard Davies, as chairman of the new Securities and Investment Board, saying it would help coordination between it and the Bank.

"It will continue to be important under the new arrangements that the central bank is able to monitor, through the new regulatory body, the condition of individual institutions, as well as that of the system as a whole," George said in a statement.

Earlier, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said the supervision of Britain's banking sector would be transferred to a new, strengthened Securities and Investment Board, which will also take responsibility for the regulatory regime covered by the Financial Services Act.
Davies, up to now the Bank's deputy governor, will head the enhances SIB.
George said banks were crucial to the British financial system because of their role as suppliers of liquidity to borrowers and depositors and their central role in payments and settlements.

As a result, their exposures to each other "make them particularly vulerable to contagion from elsewhere in the system. In this context, I welcome the goverment's intention to involve the Bank fully in drawing up the detailed proposals."

George welcomed the government's intention to use the supervisory expertise of Bank staff and the appointment of Davies "which will provide for continuity and at the same time help to ensure the necessary coordination between the SIB and the Bank in relation to their respective interests."
He also backed Brown's assertion that the distinctions between different financial institutions -- banks, insurance firms and securities companies -- were becoming blurred.
"We have never argued that banking supervision...must necessarily be undertaken in the central bank," he said.
